newsitem.title: USA: Johnson & Johnson profits rise 15 percent.
newsitem.headline: Johnson & Johnson profits rise 15 percent.

text.p: Johnson & Johnson said Tuesday that its profits expanded by 15 percent in the second quarter, paced by strong growth in domestic pharmaceutical sales.

The company, the world's largest manufacturer of health care products, said its net income for the three months ended June 30 rose to $909 million, or 68 cents a share, from $791 million, or 60 cents a share, in the previous year.

Revenue for the quarter climbed 6 percent to $5.698 billion from $5.382 billion, although the impact of the stronger dollar relative to foreign currencies decreased sales by 3.2 percent, the company said.

"While the strength of the dollar had a significant impact internationally, we are pleased with our top line growth on a local currency basis," Chairman and Chief Executive Ralph S. Larsen said in a statement.

The company, which has more than 170 operating companies in 50 countries, said its worldwide pharmaceutical sales increased by 7 percent to $1.93 billion, which included a 14 percent gain in domestic sales.
It reported a 6 percent increase to $2.15 billion in worldwide sales of medical devices and instruments, including disposable contact lenses.

Worldwide sales of consumer products increased by 4.4 percent to $1.61 billion, led by the strong performance of over-the-counter pharmaceuticals and the continued strength of skin care products, including the Neutrogena line.
For the first six months of the year Johnson & Johnson said its net income improved by 16 percent to $1.82 billion, or $1.36 a share, from $1.58 billion, or $1.19 a share.
Revenue for the six months grew by 6.5 percent to $11.4 billion from $10.7 billion.
Johnson & Johnson's stock added 75 cents to $63.69 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
